questions.question: In Pennsylvania, it is illegal for anyone under 21 to ____ alcohol.

options.text: Serve
Wear clothing advertising
Be in the presence of
Transport

questions.explanation: In Pennsylvania, anyone under 21 cannot buy, drink, or carry alcohol. You also cannot have it in your car while driving. Breaking these laws can result in losing your driving privileges.

questions.question: When a green arrow changes to a solid green light, you:

options.text: May still turn, but you must yield to oncoming traffic.
May no longer turn and must go straight.
Still have the right-of-way to turn.
No longer need to turn in the direction the arrow pointed.

questions.correctAnswerText: May still turn, but you must yield to oncoming traffic.
questions.explanation: When a green arrow becomes a solid green light, you can still turn in that direction. However, you must let oncoming traffic and pedestrians go first.

questions.question: Which statement about winter driving is false?

options.text: Winter is the hardest season for driving.
Check your antifreeze and windshield washer fluid in winter.
Using cruise control in winter weather is safe.
Snow tires help your vehicle grip slippery roads.

questions.correctAnswerText: Using cruise control in winter weather is safe.
questions.explanation: Do not use cruise control on snow, rain, fog, or other bad conditions. Winter driving is difficult and needs extra care. Check antifreeze and washer fluid levels often. Snow tires improve grip on slick roads.

questions.question: You can cross solid yellow lines:

options.text: To pass cars going the same direction.
During the day only.
Anytime.
When turning.

questions.explanation: Broken lines can be crossed, but solid lines cannot. You can only cross a solid yellow line when you are turning.

questions.question: If your vehicle's rear skids to the left, you should:

options.text: Steer left.
Apply the brakes.
Speed up.
Steer right.

questions.explanation: When your car skids on wet or icy roads, steer toward the direction you want to go. If the rear slides left, turn the wheel left. If it slides right, turn right.

questions.question: After an accident, your vehicle is blocking traffic. You should:

options.text: Move your vehicle off the road if you can.
Do not move your vehicle for any reason.
Wait for police before moving your vehicle.
None of the above.

questions.correctAnswerText: Move your vehicle off the road if you can.
questions.explanation: After a minor accident, move your vehicle off the road if possible. Always stay at the scene and give the other driver your information.

questions.question: When parking uphill on a street with a curb, you should:

options.text: Turn your wheels hard toward the curb.
Turn your wheels slightly to the right.
Turn your wheels hard away from the curb.
Keep your wheels straight.

questions.correctAnswerText: Turn your wheels hard away from the curb.
questions.explanation: Turn your wheels hard away from the curb when parked uphill. This keeps your car from rolling into traffic if the brakes fail. On streets without curbs, turn the wheels toward the edge of the road.

questions.question: When crossing a railroad track with no signals or gates, you should:

options.text: You have the right-of-way and do not need to check for trains.
You may pass slower drivers while crossing.
Make sure your vehicle can cross without stopping.
All of the above.

questions.correctAnswerText: Make sure your vehicle can cross without stopping.
questions.explanation: Before driving onto railroad tracks, check that you have enough room to cross completely. Never pass other vehicles at or near railroad crossings. Always look for trains before crossing any tracks.

questions.question: To prevent crashes, you should:

options.text: Signal and communicate with other drivers.
Ignore other drivers.
Drive only on small streets and back roads.
Avoid driving during rush hour.

questions.correctAnswerText: Signal and communicate with other drivers.
questions.explanation: Crashes happen when drivers do unexpected things. Signal when you slow down, stop, or turn. Use your horn and emergency signals when needed. This helps other drivers, bikers, and pedestrians know what you plan to do.

questions.question: When parking uphill on a street with a curb, you should:

options.text: Keep wheels straight and use the parking brake.
Turn wheels away from the curb.
Turn wheels toward the curb.
Turn back wheels into the curb.

questions.correctAnswerText: Turn wheels away from the curb.
questions.explanation: Turn your wheels hard to the left, away from the curb, when parking uphill. If your brakes fail, your vehicle will not roll into traffic.

questions.question: What should you do when you see a steady yellow arrow at a traffic signal?

options.text: Merge into the lane the arrow points to.
Slow down and stop if it is safe to do so.
Turn left after letting oncoming traffic and pedestrians pass.
You have the right-of-way. Oncoming traffic must stop for you.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down and stop if it is safe to do so.
questions.explanation: A steady yellow arrow means a red arrow is coming next. Stop unless you are already in the intersection.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: Intersection.
Road curve.
Right turn.
Lane change.

questions.explanation: This sign warns that an intersection with a crossing road is ahead.

questions.question: What should you do when driving on wet roads?

options.text: Increase your following distance to five or six seconds.
Decrease your following distance to two seconds.
Do not worry about your following distance.
Keep a four-second following distance.

questions.correctAnswerText: Increase your following distance to five or six seconds.
questions.explanation: On wet roads, increase your following distance to five or six seconds.

questions.question: You hear a siren but cannot see the emergency vehicle yet. What should you do?

options.text: Keep driving until you see the vehicle.
Pull to the curb and look to see if it is on your street.
Slow down. Do not stop until you see it.
Speed up and turn at the next intersection.

questions.correctAnswerText: Pull to the curb and look to see if it is on your street.
questions.explanation: If you hear a siren but do not see the emergency vehicle, safely pull over to the right side of the road and stop. Stay there until you are sure the vehicle is not coming toward you.

questions.question: What must you do to pass a slower vehicle on a two-lane, two-way road?

options.text: Do not cross the centerline.
Flash your lights at oncoming traffic.
Use the shoulder.
Use the lane for oncoming traffic.

questions.correctAnswerText: Use the lane for oncoming traffic.
questions.explanation: To pass on a two-lane, two-way road, you must use the lane for oncoming traffic to complete your pass. Only pass if you can do so safely and legally.

questions.question: What do round signs indicate?

options.text: No passing zones.
School zones.
Upcoming railroad crossings.
Hospitals.

questions.explanation: Round signs warn drivers that a railroad crossing is ahead. Drive carefully when you see this sign.

questions.question: What is a safe practice when driving through a work zone?

options.text: Drive close to the vehicle in front of you to keep traffic moving.
Cut your usual following distance in half.
Use cruise control.
Double your usual following distance.

questions.explanation: Rear-end collisions are the most common type of crash in work zones. Double your following distance to stay safe.

questions.question: What should car drivers know about large trucks?

options.text: They have large blind spots.
They can stop faster than passenger vehicles.
They do not need more room to maneuver than passenger vehicles.
All of the above.

questions.explanation: Large trucks have large blind spots in front, on the sides, and in the back. Avoid staying in these areas. Trucks need more room to maneuver and stop than passenger vehicles because of their size and weight.
